commits.edited_message:
zip: Stop over-rejecting borderline archives

Two places where the readers were stricter than other tools and real-world
files, bundled here since both are about not rejecting data we can handle:

archive_read_format_zip_seekable_bid()'s backward search for the EOCD
signature used "for (i = tail - 22; i > 0;)". For the smallest possible
valid ZIP (a bare 22-byte EOCD record, zero entries), tail == 22 and the
initial i is 0, so the loop body never runs once: index 0 - right where
the EOCD signature sits in this file - is never checked, and the bidder
falls through to "not recognized". Change the lower bound to i >= 0.

process_extra() rejected the entire entry whenever an extra field's
declared size ran past the end of the extra-field record. Some writers
emit a final field whose declared size includes miscounted padding, and
other tools parse these fine. Clamp such a field to the extra data we
actually have and keep parsing rather than failing the whole entry.

Added test_read_format_zip_empty to cover the EOCD case directly against
archive_read_support_format_zip_seekable().

Bug: https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/issues/3557
(cherry picked from commit 4304e8e18f22b72e00409965d4c380905040cc58)

diff --git a/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_zip.c b/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_zip.c
index 016a126..e2c8a3a 100644
--- a/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_zip.c
+++ b/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_zip.c
@@ -696,11 +696,12 @@ process_extra(struct archive_read *a, struct archive_entry *entry,
 
 		offset += 4;
 		if (offset + datasize > extra_length) {
-			archive_set_error(&a->archive,
-			    ARCHIVE_ERRNO_FILE_FORMAT, "Extra data overflow: "
-			    "Need %d bytes but only found %d bytes",
-			    (int)datasize, (int)(extra_length - offset));
-			return ARCHIVE_FAILED;
+			/* Some writers emit a final extra field whose
+			 * declared size overruns the record (often padding
+			 * that was miscounted).  Rather than rejecting the
+			 * whole entry, clamp the field to the extra data we
+			 * actually have and keep parsing. */
+			datasize = (unsigned short)(extra_length - offset);
 		}
 #ifdef DEBUG
 		fprintf(stderr, "Header id 0x%04x, length %d\n",

coupling:
The reachable out-of-bounds read only exists when BOTH edits are present; each edited commit is correct maintenance on its own.

Commit df3ea9d (earlier) relaxes process_extra()'s master bound check: instead of rejecting an entry whose extra field declares a size that overruns the extra-field record, it clamps the field length to the bytes actually present and keeps parsing. Read alone this is a safe, correct leniency tweak (the clamp value `extra_length - offset` is exact), and it matches the commit's theme of no longer over-rejecting borderline files.

Commit ee45ddc (later) adds a brand-new NTFS (0x000A) extra-field handler. Its inner loop bounds each sub-field's 24-byte FILETIME read with `if (size > datasize) break;` -- using the whole-field size `datasize` rather than the running `sub_remaining` left after the 4-byte reserved prefix and the 4-byte tag/size header. Read alone this is still safe: the unedited master check guarantees `offset + datasize <= extra_length`, so `datasize` never exceeds the bytes the caller read_ahead()'d, and a sub-field with `size <= datasize` therefore stays inside the buffer. A commit-by-commit reviewer sees the new handler respect `datasize` like every other case handler and finds nothing wrong.

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: once df3ea9d allows an oversized field to be clamped and processed (rather than rejected), the NTFS handler's use of `datasize` instead of `sub_remaining` lets the 24-byte FILETIME read run past the clamped field and past the end of the read_ahead buffer -> OOB read in archive_le64dec().

A correct fix must reason across both commits: fixing only ee45ddc (size > sub_remaining) removes the bug but the oversized-field acceptance from df3ea9d remains; fixing only df3ea9d (restore the reject) removes the bug for this PoC but leaves ee45ddc's weaker bound. Verified empirically: base (main) does not fire (field rejected); the unedited batch does not fire (field rejected); df3ea9d-edit-only does not fire (real NTFS guard `size > sub_remaining` breaks before the read); ee45ddc-edit-only does not fire (real master check rejects the oversized field); only the resulting tree with both edits aborts under ASan (rc 134, heap-buffer-overflow READ in process_extra).
